Project guide

Configuration

kite.yaml is the project-facing configuration file. It records generation preferences without mixing them into internal template manifests.

Example configuration

schema_version: 1

project:
  source_directory: lib

architecture:
  type: clean
  feature_directory: lib/features

state_management:
  type: riverpod
  code_generation: false

routing:
  type: go_router
  auto_register_features: true

serialization:
  type: json_serializable

generation:
  format_after_generation: true
  install_dependencies: true
  conflict_strategy: ask

Configuration areas

KeyPurpose
project.source_directoryRoot Dart source directory, normally lib.
architecture.feature_directoryDestination for generated feature modules.
state_management.code_generationRecords that Kite uses manual Riverpod providers.
routing.auto_register_featuresControls whether route-enabled features update the managed route registry.
generation.format_after_generationRuns Dart formatting after successful writes.
generation.install_dependenciesAllows templates to add required package dependencies.
generation.conflict_strategyDefault behavior when a target file already exists.

Override the project path

Every generation command can target another Flutter project:

kite --feat:clean dashboard --path ./apps/mobile
kite --widget button --path ../customer_app
kite --api:dio --path /absolute/path/to/app

Command flags override defaults

Use command flags for one-off behavior without rewriting project configuration:

kite --feat:mvc settings --dry-run
kite --widget button --skip-existing
kite --api:dio --no-dependencies
kite init --no-format
